# WO-2026-08-10-13 — Grounding that already exists must be found
# guidance: WO-YYYY-MM-DD-nn — slice title

## Acceptance criteria

### Warwick was asked to identify a product the catalogue already holds. Here is exactly why.

He was asked *"Which product is VANISH PRETREAT GEL?"* against a household regular literally named
**"Vanish Pre-Treat Gel"**, and got **"No candidate products found"**. His words: *"its bloody
obvious!"*

**Larry probed the real normaliser at this head. The mechanism is not a mystery:**

```
"VANISH PRETREAT GEL"  -> "vanish pretreat gel"
"Vanish Pre-Treat Gel" -> "vanish pre treat gel"
```

`termMatch.normaliseMatchText` replaces every non-alphanumeric run with a **space**, so a hyphen
*inside a word* splits it into two tokens. Warwick's unhyphenated spelling stays one token. The two
strings can never be equal, so `EXACT_ALIAS` and `REGULAR` both miss, and the approximate path
(`resolveByCatalogue.js:120-132`, words longer than 3 characters) does not rescue it either.

**This is grounding that ALREADY EXISTS and is not being found.** That is the whole defect.

### The second failure is NOT the same defect, and you must not conflate them

```
"BATCHLORS MAC N CHEESE" -> "batchlors mac n cheese"
Batchelors regular       -> "batchelors pasta n sauce mac n cheese pasta sachet 99g"
```

That one is a **misspelling** (`batchlors` / `batchelors`) plus a token-subset problem. It needs
fuzzy or subset matching, which is a different and much more dangerous change — the same suggestion
channel that got Batchelors right also offered **toothpaste for a glove request** and **tea towels
for ham**. **AC3 governs it: report, do not fix.**

### Acceptance criteria

**AC1 — A PUNCTUATION DIFFERENCE INSIDE A WORD MUST NOT CAUSE A MISS.** `"VANISH PRETREAT GEL"`
resolves to the household regular `"Vanish Pre-Treat Gel"`. The normaliser's own comment already
claims this property — *"Punctuation and spacing differences therefore cannot cause a miss"* — and
it is false for the intra-word case. Make the comment true.

**AC2 — DETERMINISTIC, NOT FUZZY.** The fix is a normalisation rule, not a similarity score, not an
edit distance, not a threshold. Two strings either agree under the rule or they do not. **If you
find yourself choosing a cutoff, you have left this order's scope** — stop and report.

**AC3 — NO NEW FALSE POSITIVES, and this is the criterion that matters most.** A wrong product costs
Warwick money and trust; a needless question costs him a tap. Prove your rule does not newly collide
any two DISTINCT products in the real household catalogue. **Report the collision count you
measured and the method** — a rule that merges two genuinely different regulars is worse than the
bug it fixes. Misspellings and token-subset matching are OUT: report them, fix neither.

**AC4 — EVERY EXISTING RESOLUTION STILL RESOLVES THE SAME WAY.** `stripLeadingQuantity` is built on
`normaliseMatchText`, and `planner.js` deliberately keeps its own narrower `normaliseTerm` for
dedupe keys and exact equality. **Establish who consumes your changed function before you change
it**, and state in your return every consumer you found and what your change does to each. If a
consumer uses it for anything data-shaped rather than matching, STOP and report.

**AC5 — REGRESSION FIRST, RED BEFORE GREEN.** A test asserting `"VANISH PRETREAT GEL"` resolves to
the `"Vanish Pre-Treat Gel"` regular. It must FAIL at this head — proving the defect is real — and
pass after. Quote both directions with executed counts.

**AC6 — MUTATION-PROVEN.** Remove your rule, prove a NAMED test goes RED, restore byte-identical
with sha256 quoted both sides. Mutate inside a `git archive` export or restore in a `finally`, and
assert the source actually changed before running.

**AC7 — NOTHING LIVE.** `live_authority: none`, `credential_scope: none`, `network: none`. Do not
connect to the live database. `SHOP-2026-08-10-M64` is preserved evidence — do not repair it.

## Required evidence

- `cd services/asdair/interpret && node --test` -> PASS/FAIL counts before and after. Measure the baseline yourself.
- `cd services/asdair/skill && node --test` -> counts before and after. NOTE: 7 failures are PRE-EXISTING at this head (Postgres/PGHOST environment cases in lastOrder.test.js, schemaCompat.test.js and assertSafeDbTarget). Report them as pre-existing by name and do not repair them.
- `cd services/asdair/pipeline && node --test` -> counts before and after (baseline 405) — termMatch is consumed beyond your surface and you must prove you broke nothing
- the AC5 regression in BOTH directions, RED at this head and GREEN after, each with executed counts
- the AC3 collision measurement: state the method and the number
- `bash scripts/secret-scan.sh --surface services/asdair/skill/termMatch.js services/asdair/skill/termMatch.test.js services/asdair/interpret/resolveByCatalogue.js services/asdair/interpret/tolerantResolve.test.js` → report exit code AND coverage. Exit 2 is NOT SCANNED, never a pass

## Inputs supplied

- `Deliverables/2026-08-10-warwick-telegram-capture-m64.md` — the actual cards, including the Vanish and Batchelors questions and Warwick's own words about them.
- `services/asdair/skill/termMatch.js:112` `normaliseMatchText` — the rule, and its comment claiming a property it does not have.
- `services/asdair/interpret/resolveByCatalogue.js:87-132` — the exact-alias, regular and approximate paths that all miss.
- `Builds/BUILD-015-.../Assurance/veritas-phase-b15-user-journey-gate2-e0667dc.md` — the Gate 2 FAIL, which cites escalation of already-grounded items.
- WP-B15-10's read-back located this file as the real fix site and correctly refused to cross into it.

## Explicitly out of scope — report, never fix

- MISSPELLINGS and token-subset matching (the Batchelors class). Report, fix neither. The same channel that got Batchelors right offered toothpaste for gloves and tea towels for ham — that is what a loose matcher does.
- Any similarity score, edit distance, threshold or curated exception list.
- `planner.js`'s own narrower `normaliseTerm` — deliberately separate for dedupe keys and exact equality. Do not unify them.
- FOUR other workers are live: `bot/**` + `pipeline/runtime.js`; `pipeline/runPipeline.js` + `deps.js` + control-plane; `skill/listNormaliser.js` + `intake/**`; `browser-runner/**`. NOTE `skill/listNormaliser.js` is another worker's file in your own directory — do not touch it.
- Repairing Warwick's live shop.

## Sequencing

1. **READ-BACK FIRST, then HOLD** (SOP-022). Restate the outcome, your proposed rule, what the order
   failed to settle, and what looks wrong. Do not implement until Larry accepts or amends.
2. **Establish every consumer of `normaliseMatchText` before changing it** (AC4) and report them.
3. AC5 regression RED first.
4. Implement the rule. Then AC3 — measure collisions against the real catalogue shape and report the
   number and the method.
5. AC6 mutation, byte-identical restore.
6. Re-run all three suites; report counts.
7. **Git endpoint: COMMIT and PUSH `build-015/b15-13-grounding-normalisation`. No PR. Do NOT touch
   `main`. Do NOT merge.**

Return: the rule you chose, every consumer of the changed function and its effect on each, the
collision measurement, both mutation directions with the sha256 pair, suite counts, and anything you
refused.
